summary:
Climate change is creating new uncertainties for agricultural systems. Shifting precipitation patterns, increasing temperatures, prolonged dry periods, and extreme weather events can affect soil conditions, crop development, and long-term agricultural productivity.
However, these challenges do not affect every farm equally. Soil composition, regional climate, water availability, and existing farming practices all influence how agricultural land responds to environmental changes.
Farmers need more than general climate predictions. They need information about the specific environmental conditions affecting their land and how those conditions should influence their decisions.
We developed GreenRevolta, an agricultural intelligence initiative designed to bridge the gap between environmental data and practical farming decisions. By integrating NASA satellite observations, soil characteristics, historical climate records, and machine learning, GreenRevolta aims to help farmers better understand the environmental conditions affecting their land.
Our platform analyzes key agricultural indicators, including precipitation, evapotranspiration, vegetation health (NDVI), soil moisture, temperature patterns, and soil composition. By examining these variables together, we can develop a more comprehensive understanding of regional environmental conditions and identify potential agricultural challenges, helping farmers make informed decisions.
details: Our website, GreenRevolta, is a useful tool for farmers around the world to make educated decisions about their land. The website can use locations from the user to get information about their area such as rainfall, dry spells, and other factors that are beneficial for farmers to understand. The website also interprets that information to show to the user. Additionally, there is a crop rotation planner where the user can give information about their land and specifics if they want such as water availability, size, soil type, pH, etc, to plan out potential sustainable crop rotation strategies as well as strengths and limitations. The benefits expand past just getting information as farmers would be able to implement the rotation ideas to improve the health of the soil to make it more sustainable for the climate as poor crop rotation can be detrimental to the environment. We used GitHub, Visual Studio, Stitch, and Render to make the website and used HTML and CSS for the UI/UX, with Python as our standard backend. Our project is very creative and unique because it brings increased education to farmers to make more educated choices which can lead to more profits and increased climatic benifets. Our team considered many factors when developing this website. To start, we ensured that the website was very user-friendly for farmers across the world to use and that the information applies worldwide. Moreover, we decided that the majority of our model was going to be dependent on a few key parameters that almost all farmers know. More specific factors could be the pH, average inclination of the land, etc. Lastly, a major consideration that we thought of was how we should present the information. We decided that all of our decisions should be fully transparent so instead of giving simple outputs, Revolta, instead gives explanations for all of the decisions and interprets all of the scientific data returned to the user so users can easily understand everything they need to know quickly and efficiently.
